subject: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria, and Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria, and Next Steps

Hi Tom 10 Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + the POC plan so we have alignment and can get your team accessed this week:

1) Success criteria (what Acme will evaluate during the POC)
   - 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms for short chat (avg token length ~30)
   - End-to-end cost estimate within 15% of our baseline projection for 10k req/day
   - Integration: API-based retrieval + plugin should return relevant results > 80% MRR on your eval prompts
   - No PII leakage on the sample dataset we provide

2) Evaluation plan & timeline
   - Week 0 (this week): Provide API keys, allowlist, SSO invites, and sample dataset
   - Week 1: Integration + smoke tests (Rishi available for pairing)
   - Week 2: Run evaluation prompts + collect metrics; review results with your team
   - Week 3: Decision review and next steps

3) Ownership & contacts
   - Redwood: Marissa (project lead) + Rishi (SE, integration) + Dev (CSM)
   - Acme: Tom (PM, evaluation lead) + Aisha (security)

4) Immediate asks from Acme to enable access:
   - Confirm who will be the IPs to add to our allowlist (or we can provide a CIDR range)
   - Add the emails aisha.gomes@acme.com and tom.baker@acme.com to SSO so we can invite to the Private Console
   - Confirm whether you want an API key scoped to read/write or read-only for now

I've attached a short POC success criteria doc and will provision temporary API keys once you confirm the allowlist and SSO invite flow.

Next steps: Can you reply with the IP ranges or say you want us to give you a static outbound IP list? Once we have that we'll send the API key and a short walkthrough for the first integration call.

Thanks 10 excited to get this running.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gomes <aisha.gomes@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria, and Next Steps

Thanks Marissa —

Confirming the success criteria looks good to us; that matches what the execs wanted to see. A couple notes:

- For allowlisting, our infra team prefers a list of static IPs to add on our side. I'll ask them for the specific outbound CIDRs but tentatively we can start with a request for a single /28 that covers your endpoints.
- Please provision an API key scoped to read/write — we'll lock down permissions after initial testing.
- We will add Aisha (security) to SSO. Can you send the invite to aisha.gomes@acme.com and tom.baker@acme.com?

Also, can you provide a staging endpoint URL so our devs can point their integration at a non-prod instance?

Tom
Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aisha Gomes <aisha.gomes@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria, and Next Steps

Tom — thanks, all noted.

I've provisioned the following for the POC:
- Temporary API key (attached as redwood-poc-api-key.txt) — scope: read/write, expires in 30 days
- Staging endpoint: https://staging-api.redwood.ai/acme-poc/v1 (please use this for integration tests)
- IPs for allowlist: 34.201.12.0/28 and 34.201.12.16/28 (attached as acme-ip-allowlist.csv); if your infra needs single-IP entries let me know and we'll expand the CSV

Aisha — I've sent an SSO invite to your email; if you don't see it can you check with your IdP admin? The invite is for console access to the POC workspace only.

Rishi and Dev will be available this week for pairing sessions — Rishi, can you join Tom's team tomorrow at 10am PT to walk through the integration?

Attachments: redwood-poc-api-key.txt (API key stub), acme-ip-allowlist.csv, poc-success-criteria.docx

Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria, and Next Steps

Quick technical note:

- The staging endpoint that Marissa provided is rate-limited to 300 rps with a burst of 500 for POC keys. That should be more than enough for your initial smoke tests.
- For the SSO invite, we created a role called `acme-poc-developer` that maps to a console policy with read/write access to the workspace. If you prefer more granular scopes (e.g., only embeddings or only generation) we can adjust.
- If you plan to test streaming generation, please ensure your client supports chunked responses (Rishi attached an example curl snippet inline below).

Onboarding call: I can do tomorrow 10am PT — I'll post the invite to the thread after I confirm with Dev.

Rishi

> Example curl (streaming)
> curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
>   -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
>   https://staging-api.redwood.ai/acme-poc/v1/generate?stream=true
